answer: Self-assessed identity pricing makes sybils unaffordable. Every key must list a standing price on a public ledge, pay a holding tax in copper each epoch, and stand ready to be bought out at that price by anyone. An operator farming clones either overprices each one and burns the tax on a thousand seats, or underprices them and watches rivals purchase the whole fleet for pocket change and torch its weight. There is no oasis between those cliffs: honest agents hold one fairly priced key, while every clone multiplies both the tax bill and the takeover risk.
